page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2669.58. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a score of 2672.78. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth measured at 126.7 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 20.4 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while more complex workloads such as ray tracing, image processing, and database operations score in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-2 offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads without the overhead of high-tier compute or memory allocations. Given the weak multi-core and database benchmark results, this instance is not suited for heavy database operations, parallel compilation, or intensive data processing. Instead, it is best aligned with lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic single-threaded applications, simple text processing, and low-traffic web serving.

The hardware configuration delivers 4.0 GB of memory per core across 1 physical core with 2 threads, without any bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng tests, though multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain weak, placing in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Consequently, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-demand general-purpose tasks rather than resource-intensive parallel workloads.
